clue.text: Go the better way to get back?

definitions.meaning: to get well again after illness is to move towards better health

explanation.surface: A riddle about whether taking the better route is how you return.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering covers both regaining health after illness and regaining something that was lost.

clue.text: Aversion that's surely to Diana's advantage

parts.note: Di is the short form of the name Diana, so Diana's is Di's
a favour is a benefit or advantage given to someone

explanation.surface: Something said to work in Diana's favour is, oddly, a sign of dislike.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Di's favour' as something in Diana's interest; 'that's surely to' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of favour, or regarding something with dislike, is a form of aversion.

clue.text: Does he count as a narrator?

definitions.meaning: a bank clerk who counts money, or a person counting votes

explanation.surface: A question whether a storyteller counts as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank cashier or vote counter has this title, and so does anyone who tells tales.

clue.text: Mark the metropolis-there's not much of it!.

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a metropolis is a big city

explanation.surface: Someone notes a big city and remarks that little of it is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortage, the state of being in short supply, is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Associate in training, unlikely to fall down?

definitions.meaning: a racehorse trained in the same yard as another
read literally, a steady, firm companion

explanation.surface: A trainee colleague who keeps their footing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses sharing one trainer's yard are so called, and the phrase also suggests a steady partner who will not topple.

clue.text: Renegade from a river nation .

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a state is a nation

explanation.surface: A deserter who comes from a country on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade abandons a faith or cause, just as a turncoat does.

clue.text: Summoned to court and seen there, I heard

indicators.note: the speaker claims to have heard it, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: sighted means seen

explanation.surface: A witness was summoned to court and, rumour says, spotted there.
explanation.definitionFit: A person named in a summons to appear before judges has been so called, in legal usage.

clue.text: Drunken servant in appropriate surroundings

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tipsy servant found in a fitting setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Pubs are just the place for a drunken servant, which is the joke of the definition; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns and pubs are the fitting setting for anyone who has been drinking.

clue.text: Resolve to throw part of the police force in to the river

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other here

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to throw a group of police officers into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to settle or determine a matter.

clue.text: Unsuccessful-because a bit over-organised?

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A failure blamed on too much planning.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt that fails to come to fruition is fruitless, unsuccessful.

clue.text: Spoon, maybe, in, a society centre

definitions.meaning: a spoon is an old name for a lofted wooden golfing implement
a club building where members gather

explanation.surface: A spoon belonging to a social centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoon was an old wooden club used in golf, and the same phrase names a members' clubhouse for golfers.

clue.text: Royal family from Stroud

indicators.note: the letters are made from a reworking of the town's name

explanation.surface: A royal line hailing from Stroud, a town in Gloucestershire.
explanation.definitionFit: The house that ruled England from Henry VII to Elizabeth I was a dynasty of monarchs.

clue.text: Wayward fashion for poets to be reimbursed?

definitions.text: fashion for poets to be reimbursed
definitions.meaning: paying a poet by each stanza or line

explanation.surface: Is paying poets by the line an odd way to do things?
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary and obstinate behaviour is wayward; a payment per line of poetry is the pun.

clue.text: Pussy with a tailless style perhaps helps change but doesn't change itself

definitions.text: helps change but doesn't change itself

parts.note: pussy is a pet name for a cat

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise
the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A cat with a cropped hairdo, a strange agent of change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts STYLE to STYL and 'perhaps' rearranges it to LYST.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, an agent that speeds a reaction while remaining unaltered is exactly this.

clue.text: Shook from the tangled boughs of Heaven and Ocean, Angels of rain and (Shelley)

definitions.text: Shook from the tangled boughs of Heaven and Ocean, Angels of rain and

parts.words: Shook from the tangled boughs of Heaven and Ocean, Angels of rain and
parts.note: a quotation from Shelley's Ode to the West Wind, completed by the missing final word

explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the last word of the line from Shelley's Ode to the West Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's line ends with the flash of electricity in a storm, paired with rain.

clue.text: Grants the power to take over island fruit

definitions.text: Grants the power to take over

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
dates are the fruit of a palm

explanation.surface: An authority handed over on an island along with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise someone officially to act is to give them a commission to govern.

clue.text: A carrier of steel

parts.note: steel here is a blade, and the limb that holds one in a fight

explanation.definitionFit: The limb that wields a blade carries steel in battle.

clue.text: Everyone needs love among conquered, people

indicators.note: the pieces go among the letters of another word

parts.note: won means conquered, gained by victory
all means everyone
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Everyone needs love among the people who have been conquered.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-speaking people of southern Belgium are an ethnic group.

clue.text: Mean to arrange a single flower

indicators.note: to arrange is to put the letters in a fresh order

parts.note: a single means one

explanation.surface: A florist intends to arrange a solitary bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The windflower is a well-known plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Swan-song of decided taste!

parts.note: a female swan is called a pen
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: A last performance that shows strong preference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swan-song' looks like one idea, a farewell; split it into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong liking or inclination for something is a decided taste.

clue.text: … to produce honey in a trance?

indicators.note: producing something means making it anew from the letters

explanation.surface: Bees produce honey as if in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees gather sugary flower fluid, which turns into honey, and the word itself means sweet drink of the gods.

clue.text: Ruddy rich-too rich!

explanation.surface: A red-faced person who is far too wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flushed complexion and an overly ornate style are both described this way.

clue.text: Plunder with the gun

explanation.surface: Robbery carried out with a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to plunder it, and the word also names a shoulder firearm.

clue.text: Pseudonym for Satan?

parts.note: Old Nick is a familiar name for the Devil

explanation.definitionFit: An informal alternative name is this; the Devil's being Old Nick is the pun.

clue.text: Just the stuff for a fling after the wedding

definitions.text: Just the stuff for a fling after the wedding

parts.words: Just the stuff for a fling after the wedding
parts.note: fling suggests a romance but means throwing paper bits over the couple

explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper are thrown over a newly married couple.

clue.text: Opening your mouth and losing your head in the shelter?

indicators.note: the head of the word 'your' is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: yawning is opening the mouth wide

explanation.surface: Someone yawns and loses their head in a shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas canopy over a shop window gives shelter from sun and rain.

clue.text: Such a 'justification for international government is nonsense

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is the closest thing to a world government
a reason is a justification

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs that the case made for world government is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of rational thought amounts to nonsense or folly.
